prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1489; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss came in from the claimant, who reports being hit while turning left at an intersection and says they were taken to hospital with a concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer, and I have logged the account as given.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone to go over the sequence of events. The description of the collision matches what they first reported, and they were clear about where each vehicle was when contact happened.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision and that the other driver was turning across their path.

Entry 4: Took a recorded statement from the other driver. Their version of the turn and the point of impact lines up with the claimant's account.

Entry 5: Photos from the scene and the tow yard show damage concentrated on the driver side front and door, which is in line with the impact described.

Entry 6: Two independent witnesses gave statements that agree on the signal phase and the direction each vehicle was travelling.

Entry 7: Requested the claimant's medical records. The concussion diagnosis fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type, and the treating notes describe symptoms consistent with that diagnosis.

Entry 8: Checked the claimant's history and found no prior injury to the head or neck area on file. No earlier damage to the vehicle appears in our records or the photos taken at the scene.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course, with regular follow-up visits that became less frequent as symptoms eased. The claimant reports steady improvement and has told the same account in every conversation so far.

Entry 10: Confirmed the policy was in force on the date of loss, the driver is named on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 11: Reviewed the repair estimate. Most of the listed damage matches the described impact, and the remaining items are being checked against the photos.

Entry 12: File is in order for settlement review. No further questions for the claimant at this time, and the claim will move to the next stage once the final repair figures are received.
